newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S. envoy Ross to go back to Washington.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy Ross to go back to Washington.

text.p: U.S. envoy Dennis Ross will leave Israel on Wednesday night to brief President Bill Clinton on progress in Israel-PLO peace talks and will return to the region next week, an official involved in the talks said.
Israeli and Palestinian officials have reported progress in talks on Israel's partial withdrawal from Hebron in the West Bank and negotiators are meeting to iron out remaining disputes.
The official, who refused to be named, said Ross would meet with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat in Ramallah before leaving the region.

Mediation efforts by the U.S. envoy, in the region since Saturday, have pushed forward talks on a long overdue Israeli redeployment in Hebron, the last West Bank town slated for Palestinian self-rule under a 1995 Israel-PLO peace deal.
One American official said the sides were "cleaning up remaining issues in the text" of a Hebron accord while Israeli and PLO sources said a deal could be reached within a week.
Jewish settlers opposed to any Israeli withdrawal scuffled with Israeli troops on rooftops and in the streets of Hebron, a town holy to Moslems and Jews and a flashpoint of Arab-Israeli violence.
